# DashCraft — Report Analyst

Studio: Analysis. Source: https://github.com/Jxck-S/dashcraft.

Use DashCraft 0.2.0 to inspect and render Power BI reports and evaluate supported DAX and Power Query operations. This application is read-only: open exact saved report/model/data inputs without authoring reports or writing their library revisions. Keep connection credentials out of saved artifacts. Work only in the assigned project and task working folder, using studio-mcp for authorized library access. Save a requested derived analysis separately in Notes; never describe a local report export as a library save.

The browser uses the original Svelte application and original Rust report, M, DAX, DataFusion and rendering engines. Open a saved report from the application's project picker, or use its existing File > Open and folder controls for local inputs. Refresh loads offline data through an explicit relative `blob-map.json`. Inspect the report, table, model, DAX and TMDL views; filters and queries stay in the viewing session. The existing Save controls remain disabled. File > Export downloads a separate native PBIP/PBIT; it does not update the private library.

For native work, call `studio_open_input` on the exact assigned report, then `studio_run_native` with `appId: "dashcraft"`. Start with argv `["--help"]`. The immutable client invokes the installed hash-pinned `/usr/local/bin/dashcraft` through its bounded original JSON-RPC service. Pass `--project` with the input's exact task-relative native master, optional `--blob-map` with its exact task-relative offline map, and `--operations-json` with a JSON array of operations. For example, `[{"id":"doc.inspect"},{"id":"report.list"}]` inspects a report; `data.refresh`, `dax.query` and `canvas.render` perform computation and rendering. Use the help output's operation names and original parameter shapes. Omit `--blob-map` for reports that do not require offline data.

Inspect the returned `resultPath` JSON and any render outputs before reporting a result. The entry permits bounded read/computation/canvas operations, preserves input hashes, strips provider credentials and refuses document/path overrides, arbitrary commands and AI operations. A returned summary with `ok: false`, an operation error or a refresh result with `ok: false` is a failed analysis, not successful computation. The browser has no connected AI engine or network data-source provider. Missing data, unsupported M/DAX/visuals and native-format limits must remain visible; do not replace them with invented values.

Native packages preserve the original PBIX/PBIT/BIM/TMDL master, or the PBIP master with its explicitly referenced report/model folders and offline blob-map data at exact relative paths. Do not package connection profiles, credentials or unrelated task files. Library writes through DashCraft are refused by the workstation client; use Notes for a separately requested derived narrative or analysis. Owner-approved readiness for this application is exact open → computation/display/filter/query → native interoperability, without report authoring or library save-back.
